title: 7AR.1 malformed CIF syntax and scalar safety
mode: Local implementation and generated fast regression controls
question: Does CIF decoding require exact four-digit parsing and preserve malformed/unrepresentable tokens without partial or invalid Unicode output?

implementation.validCif: Exactly four ASCII hex digits are accumulated into a BMP value; following suffix characters and adjacent escape tokens remain separate.
implementation.malformedCif: Malformed or truncated token spelling is preserved; observations include MalformedEscape and UnrepresentedEscape.
implementation.nulEscape: U+0000 spelling is preserved and marked UnrepresentedEscape to avoid embedded-NUL truncation in C-string consumers.
implementation.surrogateEscape: Surrogate spelling is preserved and marked InvalidUnicodeOutput plus UnrepresentedEscape; no invalid UTF-8 is emitted.
implementation.surrogatePairConvention: Adjacent high/low surrogate escapes remain literal and unrepresented; no producer-authored convention was established, so no pair-combination behavior is claimed.
implementation.strictSourceAdmission: RequireValidSource refuses malformed, NUL, and surrogate observations while tolerant import retains the text.

valid: four-digit escape followed by hexadecimal suffix

limitations.reasonUncommitted: The shared worktree contains extensive pre-existing changes; staging or committing only this source/test slice risks omitting prerequisites or including unrelated user work.
